newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia to privatise 30-50 firms with state help.
newsitem.headline: Serbia to privatise 30-50 firms with state help.

text.p: Alongside a privatisation law due for adoption by the end of June, the Serbian government aims to introduce a special privatisation programme for 30 to 50 strategically significant companies with debts exceeding 50 percent of their capital, a government official said on Tuesday.

Qualifying firms would employ more than 250 people, have an impact on other industries and have had liquidity problems for more than a year, Miroljub Hadzic, assistant to the Serbian Privatisation Minister, told a meeting of private businesses.
"It is the government's duty to reveal a list of companies of special state interest along with the adoption of the privatisation law," Hadzic said.
"Despite its limited financial resources, the state must take over those companies' debt and declare it a public debt."

Under the special programme, the state would take over the qualifying companies through debt-to-equity swaps and then sell a stake to investors. The resulting government debt would be in the region of $3-4 billion dollars, Hadzic said.

"In most cases, particularly in infrastructure systems, the state will retain a controlling 51 percent stake. But further investments are needed to upgrade infrastructure which is now inadequate for this economy's needs," he said.
"It is more than certain that Zastava (the country's only car maker) will be subject to such a programme, but also some other companies from metal-processing industries."
